newsitem.title: USA: Brown & Wood names new public finance partner.
newsitem.headline: Brown & Wood names new public finance partner.

text.p: Rumors that New York-based law firm Brown & Wood is exiting public finance are "dead wrong," the firm's managing partner said, adding that Brown & Wood named a new public finance partner just last week.
"There have been some rumors that we are getting out of public finance, and we are not," Brown & Wood Managing Partner Thomas Smith said. "We are very, very committed to it."
Smith, who was named managing partner in July, cited the naming of Christina Crosby as a partner in the firm's San Francisco office as evidence of that commitment.

Brown & Wood is restructuring as firms do occasionally, he said, and public finance is one area currently being reviewed. While some members of the firm's public finance practice may be reassigned to other areas, the number of public finance partners will not change dramatically, he said.

He declined to discuss possible layoffs or what parts of the firm would be affected. The restructuring remains "a work in progress," making it difficult to provided exact numbers at this point, he said.
"We will be moving at least one of our public finance people out of public finance and into taxable packaged products," he said.
The firm currently has more than 10 public finance partners and will likely have roughly that amount once it accomplishes the restructuring, Smith said.
